newsitem.title: USA: FTC official cannot confirm reports on Boeing, EU.
newsitem.headline: FTC official cannot confirm reports on Boeing, EU.

text.p: A Federal Trade Commission official said Wednesday he had seen press reports that the European Union may require Boeing Co to try to sell McDonnell Douglas Corp's commercial airplane unit before it merges with McDonnell.
But Bill Baer, who heads the competition bureau at the FTC, emphasized that he had no first-hand knowledge whether those reports were true.

"Based on press reports, not on any conversation I've had with my colleagues in Europe, I understand that they (EU officials) have suggested that there ought to be a period of time of six months or so in which an effort is made to find an alternative buyer for Douglas Aircraft, to see if there could be a buyer out there," he said during a news conference at the United States Information Agency's Foreign Press Center in Washington.
"If there is no buyer, Boeing would be allowed to go through and complete the purchase -- at least that's my understanding from press reports of something that's under discussion," Baer said.
In Brussels, a Boeing executive said EU competition authorities had made no such demands on Boeing, but said the concern had been raised.
"This has not been a demand of the European Commission. It's been something which has been raised," the executive told Reuters.
"We know there is an area of concern which is the size of the in-service fleet (of McDonnell Douglas). We are working on remedies to address those concerns," the executive said.
The executive said that under the procedure, any concerns are made known to the parties and the parties are free to propose remedies.
